summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update37.json → valid=true). Swept the captured source for acknowledgements of known issues (prompted by the shutdown TODO found last turn), and one lands adjacent to the snapshot-cycle record: the append path's entry loop truncates a conflicting suffix and then stores the replacement entries, and on a store failure logs the error and returns without updating the cached last log, with a comment stating that this leaves the cached last log wrong when a truncation happened above (raft.go:1537-1544). Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation for a new question, both acknowledging the known issue and showing why it is bounded where a superficially similar case is not: the previous-log check consults the cache only when the requested index equals it and otherwise reads the log store (1475-1494), a successful store resets the cached position from the last entry written (1557-1559), and the sender backs off and retries — so the stale cache lasts until the next successful write, and the path that created it is the path that repairs it. The contrast is the useful part and is stated explicitly: in the snapshot-install case the install rewrites the state machine, snapshot metadata, configurations and the log region but never the cached log position, and the leader's back-off cannot walk below its own compacted prefix, so that stale position is never repaired by the mechanism that produced it — which is why the snapshot-cycle record stands as a finding while this one closes as a bounded, acknowledged wart, and why a reviewer should not conflate the two (same symptom, different repair paths and consequences). Counterevidence kept honest: the append case needs a store failure (a fault condition) while the snapshot case needs only a legitimate divergence plus a compacted leader, so the fault assumptions are not comparable and no such claim is made; a persistently failing store leaves the follower behind for as long as it fails, the boundedness claim being about the stale cache rather than availability; and nothing was executed.
